sem_impact.name: sem_impact
sem_impact.description: Deps, dependents, transitive impact, and affected tests for one entity. Call before editing, renaming, or deleting it.
promptGuidelines: Call sem_impact before editing, renaming, or deleting an entity to see everything that could break.

sem_diff.name: sem_diff
sem_diff.description: Entity-level diff between two refs (or working tree vs HEAD): which functions/classes changed, not which lines.
promptGuidelines: Use sem_diff instead of a line diff when you need to know which entities changed, not which lines.

weave_impact_analysis.name: weave_impact
weave_impact_analysis.description: Full transitive blast radius of changing one entity -- every dependent of every dependent, not just direct callers.
promptGuidelines: Use weave_impact before a wide or risky edit to see the full transitive blast radius.

systemPromptAddendum:
The loop: outline -> choose -> read one entity -> edit that entity -> check impact. Never read a whole file.
Outline: sem_outline lists one file's entities (headings/functions/classes/keys), nested by parent, sized.
Find: sem_find looks up an entity by name across the repo; sem_grep searches text/regex across the repo.
Read: sem_read reads just that entity with a SMALL budget (1500) first -- only widen it if the result is truncated.
Edit: weave_edit is the entity-level editor -- give it the entity's full new source; it claims and releases automatically.
Impact: before editing, sem_callers lists direct call sites cheaply; sem_impact / weave_impact show the full blast radius.
For blast radius, dependency chains, or change history use sem_graph / sem_path / sem_cochange before grepping.
bash is for running things (tests, builds, git, scripts) -- never for reading or searching files. If a file has no structure, sem_outline still gives line chunks.
Batch: for several independent lookups, issue them in ONE turn -- parallel calls, or array params like sem_grep patterns=[...] -- never verify file-by-file across separate turns.
